# `xl-bench` test fixtures

`cached_values.xlsx` and `clean_values.xlsx` are **tiny, hand-authored,
synthetic** workbooks — not derived from any real spreadsheet — generated by
the committed `gen_fixture.py` (stdlib-only: `zipfile`) next to this file.
They exist so `xl-bench/tests/cached_fixture.rs` can exercise every
[`xl_bench::diff::CellStatus`] classification against a real (if minimal)
`.xlsx` package, and so `xl-bench/tests/verify_dir.rs` can drive the corpus
runner over a mixed clean/poisoned/garbage directory — all without
`xl-bench` itself depending on the `zip` crate (`zip` is approved for
`xl-io` only — see the dependency-approval policy — so this crate
cannot assemble a package in-process the way `xl-io/tests/support/mod.rs`
does).

**Regenerating:** `python3 gen_fixture.py` — deterministic (fixed zip member
order, fixed `1980-01-01` `ZipInfo` timestamps), so re-running it produces
byte-identical output for both files.

**`cached_values.xlsx` contents** (`Sheet1`, see `gen_fixture.py`'s module
docstring for the full table):

| Cell | Formula | Cached `<v>` | Exercises |
|------|---------|--------------|-----------|
| A1/A2 | literal `2`/`3` | n/a | non-formula cells excluded from the diff |
| A3 | `=SUM(A1:A2)` | `5` | `CellStatus::Exact` |
| A4 | `=SUM(A1:A2)` | `999` (deliberately poisoned) | `CellStatus::Mismatch` |
| A5 | `=NOTAREALFN(A1)` | `42` | `CellStatus::EngineUnsupported` (unknown function name) |
| A6 | `=SUM(A1:A2)` | *(no `<v>` element at all)* | `CellStatus::NoOracle` |

**`clean_values.xlsx`** is the mismatch-free counterpart: only rows A1-A3
above (literals plus the one Exact `SUM` cell), so a `verify` run over it
exits 0 and its row in `verify-dir`'s aggregate index reads "ok".

Per `xl-bench/README.md`: this harness's real oracle corpus is
proprietary and never committed — these fixtures are the opposite of that:
small, synthetic, Apache-2.0-licensed files whose entire contents are
reproduced verbatim above and in `gen_fixture.py`, kept deliberately tiny so
they are never in tension with that rule.
